_comment: The heartbeat wire contract between the seat and ss-console (ss#2287).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. On 2026-08-11 the #2280 audit found that the seat had
been emitting webhook_surface_ok + webhook_surface on EVERY heartbeat since
ss#2222 and ss-console had no column, no parser and no alert for either. The
whole warn tier was written to the wire and dropped at ingest, silently, for
as long as it had existed. Nothing could have caught it: the two halves live
in different repos and no test asserted they agree.
WHAT IT IS. Every field the PINNED overlay's shared/heartbeat.py build_payload
can put on the wire, paired with the fleet_status column ss-console stores it
in and a sample value. tests/heartbeat-field-parity.test.ts posts each sample
at the real ingest handler and fails if the column stays NULL -- so a field
listed here without a reader is a failing test, not a silent drop.
overlay_ref is the OVERLAY_REF this list was read against, and it must equal
ARG OVERLAY_REF in operator/templates/Dockerfile. That pin is the only way a
new overlay field reaches a seat, so bumping it fails this gate until someone
re-reads build_payload at the new ref and re-stamps this file. Read the
limits of that in the test's header before trusting it further than it goes.

fields._comment: The ladder's CAUSE, carried since overlay#341. Four meters drive the sticky-stop ladder and each needs a different investigation, so the level alone mislabels the incident (ashton-price, 2026-09-01: a credential failure paged as 'Cost breaker'). condition is a CLOSED vocabulary at ingest -- consecutive_tool_failures | refusal_cascade | time_budget_exceeded | cost_threshold | captain_clear, from the overlay's StickyStopCondition -- and an unknown word stores NULL; reason is the seat's free-text counter line, capped at 300 chars by BOTH sides. Pairing (a cause only ever beside a level) is the SENDER's job, so these two store independently here.
fields.name: sticky_stop_reason

fields._comment: Emitted by overlay origin/main but not by the pinned ref. The console reading AHEAD of the pin is harmless; reading BEHIND it is the ss#2287 defect, which is the only direction the local cross-check enforces.
fields.name: cron_containment

fields._comment: ss#2498, hermes-smd-overlay#292. Ahead of the pin, same as cron_containment above. Cumulative count of audit rows the seat could not persist, from the volume tally at $HERMES_HOME/.smd/audit_write_failures.tally. 0 is the load-bearing value: it is what says the writer is up and has lost nothing, and the only thing that distinguishes a quiet ledger from a broken one -- so the sample is deliberately 0 and the parity probe asserts the column is written, not that it is truthy.
fields.name: audit_write_failures

fields._comment: ss#2500, hermes-smd-overlay#292. Ahead of the pin. row_hash of the newest CHAINED audit row (sha-256 hexdigest, 64 lowercase hex); the console pins it off-Machine so a ledger cannot be rewritten without the pin disagreeing. Read in the same read-only pass as audit_rows and last_audit_ts so the head and the count always describe one moment.
fields.name: audit_head

fields._comment: ss#2500, hermes-smd-overlay#292. Ahead of the pin. COUNT(*) over audit_log, the other half of the chain pin.
fields.name: audit_rows

fields._comment: ss#2488 part 2 (overlay PR #293). Emitted by the webhook gate, which survives a gateway wedge. 1 = the seat's check could look, 0 = it could not (our blindness, paged as gateway_loop_unprovable).
fields.name: gateway_loop_ok

fields._comment: Seconds since the gateway event loop last beat. Absent (not zero) while the seat's arming latch is closed, on a Hermes pin with no loop heartbeat, and inside boot suppression -- absent is a HOLD. 0 is a real value.
fields.name: gateway_loop_age_seconds

fields._comment: The part-1 supervisor's state word (entrypoint.sh gateway_liveness_state). Closed vocabulary at ingest: armed | not-armed | starting | inert | not-watching | never-healthy | refusing; anything else stores NULL. The vocabulary is enforced in FOUR places that must move together -- entrypoint.sh (writer), the overlay's shared/gateway_loop_check.py SUPERVISOR_STATES (forwarder), src/pages/api/internal/heartbeat.ts GATEWAY_SUPERVISOR_STATES (ingest), workers/fleet-alerts/src/gateway-loop.ts (alerter) -- and each drops an unknown word to NULL, which the console holds on rather than pages on. A gap in any one of them is therefore silence, not a failure.
fields.name: gateway_supervisor_state

fields._comment: Kill-ledger lines inside the last hour. The one field a supervisor restart cannot race: the line is on the volume before the container dies, so the first beat after reboot carries it.
fields.name: gateway_restarts_last_hour

fields._comment: ss#2547, hermes-smd-overlay#309. Count of send refusals in the trailing 24h: a cron turn's EXTERNAL_SEND tool call that did not end ok, a broker CONFIRM_SEND_FAILED, or a wake that carried needs-you items and dispatched nothing to a person. 0 is the load-bearing value (the seat looked and found none), so the sample is 0 and the probe asserts the column is written, not truthy.
fields.name: send_refusals

fields._comment: ss#2547. ISO ts of the newest refusal or unsent wake in the window. The fleet-alerts Worker pages when this ADVANCES past the marker it last paged on (event-shaped, never a RECOVERED), so a routine refused daily pages daily.
fields.name: send_refusals_last_ts

fields._comment: ss#2547. Newest five events, {ts, kind: refused|unsent, routine, tool, reason}; reason is the gate's refusal text (kinds only, never a value) or the broker outcome. The page body lists these.
fields.name: send_refusals_json
